changes.question_before: How do I name the output files of an array job so each task writes to its own log file?
changes.question_after: How do I name the output files of an array job so each task writes to its own log file?
changes.reference_before: Use --output with %A (array job ID) and %a (task index), e.g. --output=logs/%x_%A_%a.out. The logs directory must exist.
changes.reference_after: Use --output with %A (array job ID) and %a (task index), e.g. --output=logs/%x_%A_%a.out.

source.quote: In output file names, `%A` expands to the array job ID and `%a` to the task index, e.g. `--output=logs/%x_%A_%a.out`.

changes.justification: Remove the directory prerequisite absent from the assigned note; %x is retained only as a copied pattern, with no definition inferred.
changes.judging_guidance: Equivalent supported wording is acceptable. The scope limitation in req-011 is not a required sentence to copy.

changes.question_before: What does the --requeue option do in an sbatch script?
changes.question_after: What does the --requeue option do in an sbatch script?
changes.reference_before: It allows the job to be put back in the queue (keeping the same job ID) if it is preempted, a node fails, or it is requeued manually with scontrol requeue. --no-requeue forbids this.
changes.reference_after: It allows the job to be put back in the queue, keeping the same job ID. A running job can be requeued manually with scontrol requeue <jobid>; --no-requeue forbids requeueing.

source.quote: A job that is requeued goes back to the queue with the same job ID. Allow it with `#SBATCH --requeue` (or forbid it with `--no-requeue`). A running job can be requeued by hand with `scontrol requeue <jobid>`. By default a requeued job overwrites its output file; add `#SBATCH --open-mode=append` to keep the earlier output.

changes.justification: Remove undocumented preemption/node-failure triggers; retain explicit permission, identity and manual command.
changes.judging_guidance: Equivalent supported wording is acceptable. The scope limitation in req-011 is not a required sentence to copy.

changes.question_before: My job's state is OUT_OF_MEMORY. What does that mean and what should I do?
changes.question_after: My job's state is OUT_OF_MEMORY. What does that mean and what should I do?
changes.reference_before: It was killed for exceeding its memory request. Request more with --mem or --mem-per-cpu.
changes.reference_after: It was killed for exceeding memory. Check the recorded state and exit code with sacct -j <jobid> --format=JobID,State,ExitCode. The supplied note does not specify a memory-request change or further remedy.

source.quote: Set a minimum acceptable run time with `--time-min`; Slurm may then shorten the time limit so the job can start earlier (backfill). Jobs killed for hitting the time limit end in state `TIMEOUT`; jobs killed for exceeding memory end in `OUT_OF_MEMORY`. Check the reason with `sacct -j <jobid> --format=JobID,State,ExitCode`.

changes.justification: Provide the documented state/exit-code diagnostic next step, not an invented memory-request remedy.
changes.judging_guidance: Equivalent supported wording is acceptable. The scope limitation in req-011 is not a required sentence to copy.
